blocks.visualArc: one held threshold situation in which the body's limits, the disappearing destination, and the thing that is still there are all asked at once
narrationEn: What if one day your body can no longer take you where you want to go?
What if you wake up and there is nowhere you want to go anyway?
And when so much of the person you used to be is gone, what is still there?
narrationZhHant: 如果有一天，你的身體再也帶你去不了想去的地方呢？
如果有一天你醒來，卻發現根本沒有想去的地方呢？
當你曾經的那個人失去了那麼多，剩下來的又是什麼？

slots.editorialFunction: Carry all three opening questions inside a single continuous situation so that what is still there lands through duration, framing, and attention rather than through a second symbolic image.

blocks.visualArc: a family observed at close range -> lives contracting around the body -> three versions of waiting
narrationEn: When I think about growing old, I don't have to imagine very much.
My grandmother had a stroke and spent more than ten years in a nursing home. She lost the ability to speak, and much of her ability to communicate with us.
After my father retired, his world gradually became smaller. He spent most of his time at home watching television. Health problems eventually made even going out difficult.
My mother began showing signs of dementia after an accident. On days when she doesn't go to a day care center, she can spend hours simply sitting in a chair.
narrationZhHant: 想到變老，我其實不用想像太多。
我奶奶中風後，在養老院住了十多年。她失去了說話的能力，也失去了很多跟我們溝通的能力。
我父親退休之後，他的世界慢慢變小了。他大部分時間待在家裡看電視，健康問題後來讓他連出門都很困難。
我母親在一場意外之後開始出現失智的徵狀。沒有去日照中心的那些日子，她可以只是坐在椅子上好幾個小時。

I don't want to grow old like that.

What if I don't get to choose?

我不想變成他們那樣。

萬一我沒有選擇的權利呢？

blocks.visualArc: disciplined attempts at control -> the realization that none of them can guarantee the outcome
narrationEn: I can exercise, watch what I eat, and save enough money for retirement. But none of these can guarantee what kind of old person I will become.

I may lose the ability to travel. I may need help getting through an ordinary day. I may no longer be able to read for hours or sit in front of a laptop working on some project that nobody asked me to do.
All of that scares me.
narrationZhHant: 我可以運動、可以控制飲食、可以為退休存下足夠的錢。但沒有任何一項能保證我會變成怎樣的一個老人。
我可能會失去旅行的能力。我可能需要有人協助我度過普通的一天。我可能再也不能長時間閱讀，或坐在筆記型電腦前做沒有人要求我做的專案。
這些都讓我害怕。
